title: Implementation record
description: What one task's implementation wrote, satisfied, inferred, and departed from. The source is in the repository and this names it rather than copying it: a copy here is the copy that stops being maintained. `inferences` is the field that makes an implementation reviewable rather than merely plausible — each entry is a decision nobody specified, and a reader compares them against what the binding permitted to find the ones that should have been questions. There is no readiness flag: foundation/0005 R5 keeps a producer from running the validator over its own output, and a field asserting the work is ready to check would be exactly that.

record_id.description: Supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

task.description: Exactly one. An implementer that took two tasks produced a record neither can be reviewed from.

binding_id.description: The binding this was implemented against, so the references consumed are recoverable.

change.description: What the file now does differently, in terms of behavior.

criteria_addressed.description: One entry per criterion of the task, including the satisfied ones. A record listing only the difficult criteria cannot be read as complete.

how.description: How the implementation satisfies it, or why it does not.

inferences.description: Every inference the binding's assumptions_allowed did not cover. An inference that would change observable behavior a caller depends on is not an inference — it is a gap, and the implementer stops instead.

divergences.description: Where the implementation departs from a reference the binding named. An empty array is a claim, made deliberately.

preserved.description: Where the task changed existing behavior, what had to keep working. Written before the change rather than reconstructed after, which would produce a list shaped by whatever happened to survive.

deferred.description: What was found and not changed, with why it was outside the task. The implementer records rather than widens.
